target_customer: Live music fans (free), monetized via ticketing referral fees, later ticketing and artist tools
problem: Fans missed concerts by their favorite artists because event information was scattered across ticket sites and blogs.
business_model: Ticketing referral fees, later direct ticketing and promoter campaigns

founders.name: Pete Finlay (born Smith)
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a two-time founder.

exit.acquirer: Warner Music Group (concert discovery); Live Nation bought remaining assets in 2018-01

competitors.name: Last.fm
competitors.what: Music community and listening data service
competitors.traction_then: Large user base generating listening data

technical_complexity.rationale: Aggregating events from many sources and matching to artists and user libraries took data engineering, but used standard web tech.

defensibility.rationale: Event database became the biggest, but data was gathered from public sources and copyable; ticketing later exposed it to Live Nation.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Songkick sued Live Nation and Ticketmaster in 2016 alleging antitrust violations; it shut ticketing in Oct 2017 and Live Nation paid a reported $110M in Jan 2018 for remaining assets.

market_need_then: Fans relied on scattered listings; TechCrunch's launch review in 2007 framed Songkick as a better way to track artists across 14 ticket sites and blogs.

branding.domain_note: Operates at songkick.com; acquisition date of domain not found

identity.voice_and_tone: Site taglines: Your city, your music; For fans, by fans

branding.community_and_virality: Large fan base (15 million users claimed by the company) but no source on merch or meme culture.

brand_strength.rationale: Recognizable consumer music brand with partner integrations; no sourced evidence of the name driving growth.

pivots.from: concert discovery funded by referral fees
pivots.to: direct ticketing, then CrowdSurge merger in 2015-06
pivots.why: Extend revenue beyond ticket referrals; reason as inferred from TechCrunch headline, not company statement

outcome_analysis: Songkick built the largest concert database and about 15 million users, then moved into ticketing and merged with CrowdSurge in 2015. It sued Live Nation and Ticketmaster in 2016 over blocked US ticketing, closed ticketing in October 2017, sold the discovery business to Warner in July 2017 and remaining assets to Live Nation in January 2018 for a reported $110M. Incumbent power in ticketing capped the original plan, though the founders and investors had exits.
notes: Series A (Dec 2008, about $4M, Index Ventures) and later rounds (2015 Series C about $16.7M, 2016 about $15M led by Access Industries) appear only on aggregators (ZoomInfo, StartupIntros) and are unverified; no Series A is recorded. Totals vary from $17M at 2012 per TechCrunch to $58.7M per an aggregator. Live Nation $110M is reported. WMG sold Songkick to Suno in Nov 2025 per Wikipedia. Matt Jones (CrowdSurge) is a later co-leader, not a founder per the YC page. Competitor set limited to what the 2007 TechCrunch review contrasted; Upcoming.org and Eventful not confirmed.
